title: Concept Direction Drift Across Fine-Tuned Variants of One Base Model

original_idea.body:
# Concept Direction Drift Across Fine-Tuned Variants of One Base Model

**Problem:** A concept direction extracted from one fine-tuned variant is assumed to transfer to siblings, but fine-tuning's effect on direction geometry is rarely measured.

**Direction:** Take a base model and 2-3 public fine-tuned variants (instruct, RLHF, uncensored). Extract the refusal/toxicity direction in each; measure pairwise cosine similarity and cross-variant steering transfer.

**Why it matters:** Uncensored community fine-tunes are a real safety phenomenon; showing how fine-tuning displaces safety directions reveals whether probes generalize across descendants.

**Relevant context:** Arditi et al. 2024; abundant public Llama/Qwen fine-tunes.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: whether safety directions survive fine-tuning (incl. uncensored variants) determines if safety probes generalize across the open ecosystem.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Difference-of-means across base+variants; guided, mentor helpful for matching layers/variants.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: pairwise cosine similarity + cross-variant steering transfer.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Studies an open-fine-tune ecosystem labs don't control; needs no internal access, third-party-relevant.

low_compute.reasoning: Difference-of-means inference over a few variants, one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Concept-direction drift across fine-tuned siblings appears under-studied.
